what_its_for: Delafloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including skin and skin structure infections (such as wounds, abscesses, or cellulitis) and pneumonia (lung infection) acquired in the community. It works by killing or stopping the growth of bacteria that are causing your infection.
how_to_take: Delafloxacin comes as a tablet you swallow by mouth, or as an injection given into your vein (IV) by a healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital. Take the tablet with or without food. Swallow it whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Finish all of your medication even if you start feeling better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 450 mg (one tablet) taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart, for 5 to 14 days depending on your infection. Your doctor may give you an IV dose of 300 mg twice a day if you are receiving treatment in a hospital. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose and how long to take it.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 8 hours away. If your next dose is less than 8 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in a dry place away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package. Dispose of unused medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids, vitamins, or supplements that contain aluminum, magnesium, calcium, iron, or zinc within 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking delafloxacin, as these can make the antibiotic less effective. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds — this medication can make your skin more sensitive to the sun, so use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, confused, or have vision problems while taking this medicine. Avoid taking other antibiotics or medications unless your doctor or pharmacist approves them.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: severe tendon pain, swelling, or a snapping feeling in any joint (this could mean a tendon tear — stop the medicine right away); numbness, tingling, weakness, or unusual sensations in your limbs; fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat; severe or worsening skin rash, blistering, or peeling; mental health changes such as anxiety, depression, confusion, hallucinations, or thoughts of self-harm; watery or bloody diarrhea, which may occur even weeks after finishing the antibiotic; severe allergic reaction signs such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; worsening symptoms or signs that your infection is not getting better after a few days.
when_it_works: Most people begin to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting delafloxacin. However, it is very important to keep taking all of your doses for the full length of time prescribed, even if you feel better sooner. Stopping too early can allow bacteria to continue growing, which may cause your infection to come back or become harder to treat.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution. Older adults may be at higher risk for side effects, including tendon problems and heart rhythm changes. Tell your doctor if you are older or have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Kidney problems: Your doctor may need to change your dose if you have moderate to severe kidney disease or are on dialysis. Pregnancy: It is not known if delafloxacin is safe during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Discuss with your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Children: Delafloxacin is not currently approved for use in patients under 18 years of age.
